# IsCooked

> A local security scanner for Ollama, LM Studio, and self-hosted AI setups.

## Run the scanner

The canonical Bash source URL is https://iscooked.com/iscooked.com.

The homepage shows a static example report. It does not start the scanner. Start
the scanner in a terminal.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://iscooked.com/iscooked.com | bash
```

To download and read the source before execution:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://iscooked.com/iscooked.com -o iscooked.com &&
less iscooked.com
```

After you read the source, start it with the Bash 4 or later executable you selected:

```bash
bash iscooked.com
```

Requires Bash 4 or later and standard Unix tools. Some macOS installations use Bash 3.2. Use
Bash 4 or later on macOS. Run `bash --version` to examine the version. Python 3 is optional for structured configuration,
API, browser, and model-code checks; curl is needed for HTTP probes. Missing
optional tools cause skipped checks. Elevated privileges can improve some
firewall and port checks. The scan runs locally and does not send scan results
to a remote service. AI service probes target localhost or their local bind
addresses. The telemetry check reads opt-out variables and exact known
`0.0.0.0` entries in `/etc/hosts`; it does not inspect all outbound connections.

Older pages may advertise /i. That path is a compatibility redirect to the
canonical script URL above; use the canonical URL in new instructions.

## Reports

After download, run `bash iscooked.com --help` for options without a scan.
Use `--json` for a structured report (requires Python 3), or `--no-color` for text without terminal colors.
Use `--fail-on critical`, `--fail-on warning`, or `--fail-on unknown` to select a failure exit policy.
Without a policy, a completed scan returns 0 regardless of findings. Invalid options and unsupported requirements return 2.
Skipped results do not trigger a failure exit. A successful exit does not prove that the system is secure.

Reports count critical, warning, passed, unknown, and skipped results separately.
The terminal summary shows a colored bar, a `% cooked` score, and a score label.
The labels are LOOKING FRESH, SLIGHTLY WARM, MEDIUM RARE, and FULLY COOKED.
Critical findings and warnings cannot receive LOOKING FRESH. Reports without passed, warning, or critical results use STILL DEFROSTING.
Low scores with unknown or skipped results also use STILL DEFROSTING when no risk findings occur.
Critical findings receive a separate instruction at every score. The score is a heuristic total, not a probability.
Scanner environment values do not establish the settings of a running service.

## Links

- [Homepage](https://iscooked.com/): Static overview, checks, and example output.
- [Unknown results](https://iscooked.com/unknowns): Diagnostic steps and limits for incomplete checks.
- [Bash source](https://iscooked.com/iscooked.com): The scanner, not an HTML page.
- [Repository and README](https://github.com/johnpippett/iscooked): Requirements,
  usage, scoring, and source code.
